newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee at 11-week low as funds sell.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee at 11-week low as funds sell.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures took a pounding on Tuesday on fund long liquidation and stop-loss selling.
Benchmark September hit an intraday-low of $1,635 a tonne, a 5.8 percent fall on the day, before ending morning trade $97 down at $1,638.
This was the lowest level in 11 weeks. The slide was accelerated by Asian origin selling, traders said.
"It's all fund selling and there's no buying around," said one floor trader.
The September contract slipped through the previous major support at $1,695. This triggered sell-stops and long liquidation by funds and specs.
Further sell-stops were seen at around the $1,650s.
Volume was quite large at 7,877 lots, with September accounting for just over 5,000 lots.
Traders were unable to pinpoint specific fundamental reasons behind the sharp falls, which have taken the market to the late-April lows of around $1,610 basis September.
The winter weather in Brazil's coffee areas remained mild, with no frost forecast through July 22, while coffee stocks in the United States were building up again.
Chartwise, the next key support was pegged at the triple bottom of around $1,610.
Coffee had seen a blistering five-month rally since early January on tight nearby availabilities. The rally peaked at $2,700 in late May before it fizzled out.
On the news front, traders said LIFFE certified stocks rose to 2,346 five-tonne lots at end-June from 881 in May. The jump was within expectations.
The key U.S. green stocks data for June were due after the close of New York trading on Tuesday.
Broker GNI said estimates had been unreliable for the past few months, but the current range of expectations was from 200,000 bags up to 100,000 down.

Stocks fell by 110,000 tonnes in June last year. "It is fair to say any increase in stocks will either represent stocks from Colombia or Europe, it would however be going against the seasonal norm," it added.
